title: I've been using AI to make games for my brother since early 2025
author: acrolicious
selftext:
My brother Ben has a rare condition, and he's always loved video games. Around the time he turned 20, his condition worsened to the point where he lost the use of his hands, and gaming slowly slipped away from him.

He was super into sports games growing up, and Wii Golf was a big one for him as a young teenager. Gaming was his way to escape into a world where he had abilities he didn't have in real life, where he could win world championships, and I loved that technology gave him that. Watching it get taken away from him was really hard, and some days it still is.

When Ben moved in with us, we started using AI to build games he could play independently with two buttons mounted near his head. The minigolf game in this video is one of those, and it's pretty incredible to see how far it's come. It's given Ben back a huge chunk of his life that had been missing for a long time.

Minigolf has been through a lot. It started as a Python app, moved to HTML5, and has now been rebuilt in Three.js. It was the first thing I built as an engine rather than a single game, because it needed to be dynamic. Even that original Python app had a course editor that let you export your own courses as JSON, kind of like the track builder in Excitebike. That idea became a core principle for a lot of what we make: most of our games come with an editor, so the experience can be shaped around the player and their needs, whether that means making it easier or more challenging.

Everything we've learned and built comes from a markdown file we wrote around Ben's exact needs. It covers many accessibility standards and keeps growing as we add new features and discover gaps, but most importantly, it works for Ben.

Switch access has been around for years, but we haven't found anything that works quite like this: a complete library of custom games, communication tools and streaming, all in one interface that Ben can navigate and understand on his own.

All of it is online for free and open source, so others can use it or build off of it. We're going to keep adding to it and keep showing people how AI can help with something like this.

From our family, thanks for reading. If you know a family, a therapist, or someone who might benefit from this, we'd love for you to share it so more people can discover it.

comments.author: acrolicious
comments.body:
I know I've posted recently 😊 

Thanks for checking this out! Here's where everything lives if you want to try it or build on it:

**Play minigolf:** https://narbehouse.github.io/bennyshub/apps/games/NARBEMINIGOLF/index.html
The game from the video, playable in your browser with two switches (or just the spacebar and enter keys).

**Benny's Hub:** https://www.bennyshub.com
The full system Ben uses every day, with games, communication tools and streaming in one switch-accessible interface. It runs in the browser on Windows, Mac, Linux, Android and iOS.

**SwitchedGames:** https://www.switchedgames.org
Our library of free switch-accessible games.

**Free game dev guides:** https://narbehouse.github.io
Our open guides for anyone who wants to build accessible games with AI.

**Source code:** https://www.github.com/NARBEHOUSE
Everything is open source under the MIT license.

If you have questions or want help getting set up for someone in your life, just ask in the comments.

comments.body: What! This is so cool! I want to make a game for Ben! Thanks for sharing these resources, I’m excited to look into them and experiment.

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body: You can submit games on https://switchedgames.org/#submit-games

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body: He likes sports games but he used to love playing Spiderman on PlayStation and GTA. It's hard to figure out how to make a 2 button GTA so I'm making a Spider-Man/Hero RPG style game that's all story driven with choice / turn based fights scenes. It's ambitious but I think he might like it.

replies.author: sunnystormy64
replies.body: Have you thought about hosting a gamejam with the constraints you've mentioned? Might be an opportunity to see how far that paradigm can be pushed.

replies.author: acrolicious
replies.body:
I would love for someone to do that. Unfortunately, we can't really commit to scheduling stuff like that for various reasons- it's hard to get anyone willing to get involved so we just make stuff ourselves with a tight group over time. 

We have a full MD file that gives agents everything they need to build within the constraints. At this point, it's very easy to prompt within a fork of BennysHub.

It may be that not all game modes work but I'm hoping tone of them do. If so I'll send over a free steam key when done

replies.body: Yeah, we have an LLC but we don't make any money (very little from Socials which we donate back to our nonprofit) 😂 the nonprofit is purely volunteer and we use all the funds toward making some games and donating switches to families and professionals all around the country. It's very rewarding.
